item.title: PNG commits K25 million to assist Tuvalu
item.description: Papua New Guinea has pledged K25 million over the next five years to support Tuvalu’s efforts to protect its coastline and reclaim land threatened by rising sea levels. Prime Minister James Marape announced this today at a joint press conference with Tuvalu Prime Minister Feleti Teo, shortly after arriving in Funafuti.
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea has pledged K25 million over the next five years to support Tuvalu’s efforts to protect its coastline and reclaim land threatened by rising sea levels.

Prime Minister James Marape announced this today at a joint press conference with Tuvalu Prime Minister Feleti Teo, shortly after arriving in Funafuti.

Marape said Papua New Guinea would provide K5 million annually through its national budget to assist Tuvalu’s climate adaptation efforts.

The first payment of K5 million has already been transferred to Tuvalu’s Treasury to enable immediate work on coastal protection measures.

He announced this during the leaders’ segment of the pre-COP31 planning meetings, where Pacific leaders are discussing regional climate challenges ahead of the global climate summit.

Marape said the funding would be directed towards the Tuvalu Coastal Adaptation Project, a national initiative aimed at strengthening vulnerable coastlines and reclaiming safe land as the country grapples with the impacts of climate change and sea-level rise.

“This is an indication that whilst we wait for everybody else to respond, let’s do what we must do,” Marape said.

He also indicated Papua New Guinea’s readiness to provide additional assistance, including rock boulders and soil from its mountainous regions, should Tuvalu require physical materials for land reclamation projects.

Welcoming the contribution, Prime Minister Teo said the funding would play a significant role in protecting Tuvalu’s highly vulnerable coastline from ongoing erosion and sea-level rise.

“Declarations alone cannot physically fix eroding coastlines without substantial capital and resources,” he said.

While acknowledging recent international commitments on climate action, Teo noted that political declarations alone are insufficient to address the urgent challenges facing low-lying island nations.

item.title: London Broncos finish on high
item.description: London Broncos completed their 2026 season as champions of the Betfred Championship after defeating Doncaster 78-6 in the grand final. The 72-point victory also went down as the biggest ever grand final winning margin in the history of the championship, adding to the accolades achieved by the club this year, including winning the League Leaders’ Shield and the 1895 Cup.
item.content:encoded:
London Broncos completed their 2026 season as champions of the Betfred Championship after defeating Doncaster 78-6 in the grand final.

The 72-point victory also went down as the biggest ever grand final winning margin in the history of the championship, adding to the accolades achieved by the club this year, including winning the League Leaders’ Shield and the 1895 Cup.

Crossing the try line 14 times, it was one way traffic from the get go for the Jason Demetriou-coached outfit, with tries from Jimmy Meadows (8, 16), Dean Hawkins (12), Neil Tchamambe (26, 46), Robert Mathias (33), Elliot Wallis (37, 69), Savili Havili (40), Brandon Webster-Mansfield (42, 50), Connor O’Beirne (53), Gairo Voro (66) and Emarly Bitungane (75).

For the goal kicking, Jimmy Meadows kicked 6 from 9, Dean Hawkins kicked 0 from 1, Gairo Voro had a perfect 4 from 4 while Perth Bears bound Luke Smith kicked 1 from 1 right on full time.

The lone try from Doncaster in the second half came from Luis Johnson with Conor Robinson adding the extras to avoid the egg.

The grand final win brings London’s total number of major titles to six across their 46 seasons, including their periods as Fulham, Fulham Bears, London Crusaders, London Broncos and Harlequins RL.

Their previous titles were the 1982–83 Division Two Championship, the 2018 Million Pound Game and the 2023 Million Pound Game.

The Broncos also finished the season averaging more than 60 points per game across 34 matches.

Coach Jason Demetriou described the 2026 season as remarkable with the club achieving various milestones.

London Broncos Co-Owner Darren Lockyer said the achievements in 2026 reflects on the amount of hardwork put in by many behind the scenes.

item.title: Komkui school builds its own future
item.description: Parents of St Mark’s Komkui Primary School in Mt Hagen have shown what can happen when people take action for their children. For three years, the school worked with parents and the local community to build a spike fence and a new water supply.
item.content:encoded:
Parents of St Mark’s Komkui Primary School in Mt Hagen have shown what can happen when people take action for their children.

For three years, the school worked with parents and the local community to build a spike fence and a new water supply.

The two projects are worth almost K120,000.

The projects were officially opened by Hagen Open MP William Duma who was accompanied by Western Highlands Governor Wai Rapa, PEC members, community leaders and educated elites from Komkui.

School headteacher Mr. Apa says the parents made the projects possible by paying the school’s project fees.

“Our parents have supported us by paying the project fees. Through their support, we were able to build the spike fence and also work on the water supply. We really thank them for supporting the school.”

The school’s old water source had worn out, leaving students and teachers to depend on tank water.

The school then sourced water from a nearby mountain and pumped it into the school.

It now has clean and fast-flowing water.

Michael William also volunteered his time to help build the spike fence.

He says communities should not always wait for government assistance.

“We should not always wait for the government. We can start something ourselves. When we take the first step, the government can also come in and support us," Mr. William the contractor of the spike fence said.

That initiative has now been followed by further government support.

Hagen Open MP William Duma announced K300,000 from the Mt Hagen City Authority for St Mark’s Komkui Primary School.

“Since this school is in my electorate, I am very pleased to hear that the people are doing their own projects. When our people take the initiative, government must also respond and support them," Duma stressed.

The Western Highlands Provincial Government has also given the school K100,000.

Governor Wai Rapa said parents and other stakeholders must continue to support schools in their communities.

“When parents and the community take part in supporting their schools, it shows that they value education and can also look after the schools in their communities.”

Governor Rapa also committed one classroom from the four classrooms being supported through DFAT.

The two projects of St Mark's Komkui Primary School was officially opened by MP Duma.

" Tonight on Wednesday the 30th day of September 2026 at exactly 7:15p.m, I officially declare the Komkui school water supply and spike fencing open. May God bless the Komkui community, the teaching staff, the children of Komkui school. Thank you."

item.title: Drought destroys Zumara school toilets
item.description: A prolonged dry spell in Markham District has now damaged a basic necessity at Zumara Primary School after the school’s toilet facility was destroyed by fire. The toilet at the school in Umi LLG was burnt down during the extended dry conditions, leaving students and teachers without adequate toilet facilities and raising concerns about sanitation.
item.content:encoded:
A prolonged dry spell in Markham District has now damaged a basic necessity at Zumara Primary School after the school’s toilet facility was destroyed by fire.

The toilet at the school in Umi LLG was burnt down during the extended dry conditions, leaving students and teachers without adequate toilet facilities and raising concerns about sanitation.

The impact of the dry season is also being felt by communities around Zumara, Mitzing, Warus, Marafau, Umi LLG Chamber, and Ngaruchaniang, where families are facing shortages of water and food.

For students at Zumara Primary School, the loss of the toilet adds another challenge to daily learning as the school community struggles with the effects of the prolonged dry conditions.

Community members are now calling on the Government, Morobe Provincial Administration, Markham District Development Authority, and Umi LLG to respond to the situation and help the school restore its toilet facilities.

The community says the situation goes beyond the school, with the prolonged dry season placing pressure on students, families, and communities across Umi.

item.title: Serious consequences for malpractices in exams
item.description: Students and schools caught engaging in malpractices during the National Examinations will face serious consequences. This stern warning was issued by Education Secretary Dr. Uke Kombra in a statement.
item.content:encoded:
Students and schools caught engaging in malpractices during the National Examinations will face serious consequences.

This stern warning was issued by Education Secretary Dr. Uke Kombra in a statement.

Consequences drawn to be applied to those caught in the act include; non-certification for students, termination from teaching for teachers, and banning of schools for a minimum period of three years.

“To uphold integrity, strict supervisory guidelines have been issued to external invigilators across all provinces,” Dr. Kombra said.

Adding to this, the secretary is also encouraging members of the public, parents and students to report any suspected examination malpractice or paper leaks to the Department of Education.

According to the online student data collection system, more than 279,000 students will sit for the 2026 National Examinations with 84, 596 Grade 10s sitting for exams from October 5 th to 9 th , 37, 430 Grade 12’s from October 12 th to 16 th and 157,500 Grade 8’s sitting for exams from October 19 th to 22 nd .

item.title: Teachers shape Markham’s future
item.description: For teachers at Waritzian Primary School, teaching is more than standing in front of a classroom. It is about shaping young lives, building confidence and preparing children in Markham District for the future.
item.content:encoded:
For teachers at Waritzian Primary School, teaching is more than standing in front of a classroom.

It is about shaping young lives, building confidence and preparing children in Markham District for the future.

That message was highlighted today as the school joined communities across Papua New Guinea to mark World Teachers’ Day, recognising the dedication of teachers who continue to educate and care for children.

Teachers, students and members of the school community gathered to acknowledge the work of educators and the important role they play in their students’ lives.

The school’s motto, “Hard Work Pays,” reflects the values teachers are encouraging in their students — hard work, discipline and a commitment to learning.

For the Waritzian school community, Teachers’ Day was, therefore, not only a celebration, but an opportunity to recognise the people helping to build the next generation of Markham.

World Teachers’ Day is observed on October 5 each year.

item.title: More than 5000 grade ten students sit for final exam in Madang
item.description: A total of 5,145 nominated grade ten students are writing their final examination papers in Madang Province this week. Provincial Education Director Alphonse Igag explained these are students who have been issued their candidate's number by the Department of Education.
item.content:encoded:
A total of 5,145 nominated grade ten students are writing their final examination papers in Madang Province this week.

Provincial Education Director Alphonse Igag explained these are students who have been issued their candidate's number by the Department of Education.

Mr Igag said that despite the ongoing El Nino period, the grade ten examination is time bound, and there is no alternative but to start today, Monday 5th October.

"This is a fixed activity, so despite the challenges posed by El Nino and the unavailability of examination funds, the examinations still proceed. Madang Province has 36 secondary and high schools sitting the 2026 National Grade 10 Examinations," he said.

He said districts like Middle Ramu and Gama Local Level Government in Usino/ Bundi, which do not have road connection to the provincial capital, their leaders have hired helicopters to airlift the examination materials to their schools.

"The Madang Provincial Education authorities acknowledge the support of the Member for Middle, Kansol Harwai Kamdaru and his District Development Authority for the ongoing support over the years towards the successful delivery of examinations to grades 10 and 12 students during this time of the year.

"We also extend our gratitude to other MPs and their DDAs for their support as well.

The Madang Provincial Examinations Supervisor for Grade 10 Examinations, Darren Seming has kept school principals well informed of Examinations dates, collection and distribution of examination packages, supervision arrangements between neighboring schools and collection of examination papers after the completion, and dates to return the examination scripts.

School principals have responded positively and have ensured that examination papers have been stored in secured places before commencing today.

Mr Igag said the Education Division does not anticipate any major hiccups to the start of the examinations.

"We wish every grade 10 student in Madang Province and throughout PNG every success in the 2026 National Grade 10 Examinations," he added.

item.title: Hela parents urged to prioritize children’s education
item.description: Parents across Hela Province, particularly fathers, have been strongly urged to shift their financial priorities away from costly community expectations and focus instead on investing in their children's education. ​The call was made by John Tipa, a board member of Hela Education Services and the Provincial Election Manager, who cautioned that spending valuable resources on traditional obligations
item.content:encoded:
Parents across Hela Province, particularly fathers, have been strongly urged to shift their financial priorities away from costly community expectations and focus instead on investing in their children's education.

​The call was made by John Tipa, a board member of Hela Education Services and the Provincial Election Manager, who cautioned that spending valuable resources on traditional obligations solely to gain social standing yields no long-term security.

​Mr. Tipa emphasized that significant sums of money are routinely funneled into community events, such as house cries, funeral gatherings, compensation demands, and social contributions at the expense of basic educational needs.

​"Parents, especially fathers, like to contribute heavily to funeral services, compensation, and other community obligations," Mr. Tipa stated. "That money and those resources spent unnecessarily should be spent on their children's needs, such as clothing and school supplies."

He pointed out that while traditional contributions may offer fleeting social prestige, educating children provides a sustainable safety net for parents in their later years. Furthermore, he noted that building a generation of educated local professionals is essential for driving economic growth and social progress across Hela Province and Papua New Guinea.

​While acknowledging the provincial government's efforts under Governor Philip Undialu to subsidize school fees and upgrade educational infrastructure, Tipa stressed that public intervention must be met with equal commitment at home.

​"When the government is doing so much for the students, parents must also do their part and not depend on everything from the government," he warned, calling on parents to eliminate dependency and take full accountability for their households.

"Parents must not be lazy and dependent; they are responsible for their children's education," he said.

​Mr. Tipa challenged parents across the province to step up as responsible guardians by making their children’s academic future their ultimate priority.
